notes:
Account summary: NebulaGrid builds an edge analytics fleet for industrial plants — real-time telemetry parsing + anomaly detection. They're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable per-facility throughput and a VPC deployment model. Key asks: guaranteed minimum throughput per GPU, p90/p95 latency SLOs for seq lengths up to 1024, and long-term reserved GPU planning for seasonal peak loads.

POC scope and acceptance criteria:
- Duration: 2-week Dedicated POC (dedicated pool access + monitoring).
- Tests: ramped load tests (0->peak), 6-hour soak tests at 70% and 90% GPU utilization, and intermittent spike tests (burst to 150% with autoscaling fallback).
- Targets: sustain 2000 concurrent streams per 8-GPU pod for short-form telemetry (avg tokens per request 80); p95 latency <= 200ms for seq<=512 and p95 <= 350ms for seq up to 1024.
- Cost guardrails: Redwood to provide expected cost per 1M tokens at configured batching/quantization profile; customer wants modeling for steady-state + 3x seasonal peak.
- Security: must pass SOC2 questionnaire items #2,#5; KMS support and audit logs required; data residency for EU-managed sites.

Representative prompts used for benchmarking (shortened):
- "Parse telemetry packet: extract sensor id, event type, normalized value, timestamp; if invalid checksum mark ERROR and drop."
- "Given last 10 sensor readings, predict whether anomaly will occur in next 30s and list top 3 contributing signals with confidence."
- "Embed device diagnostic report for similarity search against historical failure corpus."

Load/soak test notes and metrics so far:
- Test harness: Redwood qps-runner v1.3 (attached drive), custom telemetry generator (10k devices emulated).
- Baseline (4xA100 equiv, batch config B3): steady 6-hour soak at 70% util -> p95=170ms (seq512), throughput 2.1k concurrent streams. Memory KV cache hit ~22% after warmup.
- Spike test: momentary burst to 3k streams -> tail p99 spikes to 980ms; automatic fallback to smaller model variant succeeded, degraded quality acceptable per product team.
- Observed tuning levers: increasing prefix caching to 40% reduces p95 by ~25% on repeated multi-turn sessions.

SLA / commercial negotiation points to resolve:
- Explicit throughput guarantee: customer requests a written minimum tokens/sec per reserved GPU and credit-based remediation for breaches. Redwood has template SLA but needs to specify remediation (service credit bands) tied to p95 latency and sustained throughput.
- Reservation sizing: NebulaGrid expects to reserve 32 GPUs across 4 regions with burst pool of 8 GPUs — need Redwood to confirm placement and autoscale latency impact.
- Pricing: prefer blended committed rate with tiered overage; wants a 12-month contract window and option to add mid-term GPU increments with 30d notice.

Action items (owner):
- SE (Maya Lin): deliver second-run soak with adjusted batching (B4) and updated KV cache config by 2024-12-18.
- AE (Jordan): circulate SLA draft with explicit throughput credit bands by 2024-12-16 (done: draft v1 attached).
- Security: complete outstanding questionnaire items and KMS integration checklist by 2024-12-19 (drive link).

Quotes / voice notes from execs:
- "If you can guarantee throughput under sustained industrial load, we can consolidate 3 regions onto Redwood." — CTO, NebulaGrid.
- "Latency consistency is non-negotiable for our control loops." — Head of Product.

Next meeting: Exec review + legal (contract review) scheduled 2024-12-20. Main blocker remains formal throughput guarantee language and final reserved GPU placement confirmation.
